clue.text: Wanted to see a schoolmaster in action

indicators.note: in here means the schoolmaster is placed inside the word for action

parts.note: an action is a deed
pupils address a schoolmaster as sir

explanation.surface: Someone was summoned to see the headmaster, who was busy at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'to see' only link definition and wordplay; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wanted is longed for, a synonym.

clue.text: Fierce woman filled with love for cavalryman

indicators.note: filled with says the fierce woman's word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a dragon is slang for a fierce, formidable woman
love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A formidable woman turns out to be full of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filled with' puts O inside DRAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon is a mounted soldier, historically a cavalry trooper.

clue.text: He pokes fun at a pig

definitions.meaning: a greedy eater, one who wolfs food down

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is both to mock and, informally, to eat greedily, so the agent noun covers a mocker and a glutton.

clue.text: Material evidence that a space-gun is working?

parts.note: a ray gun is the space-gun of science fiction, so a ray
on means switched on, operating

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what proves a science-fiction ray gun is firing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evidence that' is a link: the words read as RAY ON, the ray being on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic textile, an example of fabric.

clue.text: Newly initiated as food consultant

indicators.note: newly suggests the word initiated is made afresh, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has just been admitted as a nutrition adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly' shuffles INITIATED; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian advises people on nutrition, the expert on what they eat.

clue.text: Disturbed by a gun-toting rookie

parts.note: a rookie is a learner, L as on a learner driver's plate
carrying a gun is being armed

explanation.surface: Someone was frightened by a novice carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbed here means frightened or anxious, a synonym.

clue.text: Quick drink around teatime

indicators.note: around says the drink's word wraps the other piece

parts.note: ale is a drink
teatime is four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A quick beverage taken in the late afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: British teatime is traditionally about four o'clock. 'Quick' is the old sense, as in 'the quick and the dead'; 'around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its archaic sense means living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.

clue.text: A foretaste of peas cooked with tripe

indicators.note: cooked signals the letters of peas and tripe are mixed together

explanation.surface: A starter made from peas and tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' shuffles PEAS and TRIPE together; 'of' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser is a small dish before a meal, giving a first taste of what is to come.

clue.text: Mother conceals a blemish with some make-up

indicators.note: conceals says mother and a wrap the blemish between them

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A mother hides a skin flaw with cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' signals that mother and 'a' sit either side of the blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic for the eyelashes, an example of make-up.

clue.text: He lives comfortably in the German environment

indicators.note: in says the word for comfortably sits within the German article

parts.note: der is German for the
living comfortably is living well

explanation.surface: A man lives comfortably in German surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'environment' is a link completing the picture of German surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is a resident, one who lives somewhere.

clue.text: Terribly annoyed, so need soothing

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word annoyed is badly disordered

explanation.surface: Someone is very annoyed and needs calming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' shuffles ANNOYED; 'so need' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne remedy relieves pain, so it is calming.

clue.text: Deadlock occurs because I am out of date

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
passé means no longer fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone explains a stalemate by admitting they are behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occurs because' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation with no way forward, a stalemate.

clue.text: Assault is disgusting

explanation.surface: An attack is horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a military attack, and something offensive is repugnant.

clue.text: Lag behind right in the rear

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for right is put inside the word for rear

parts.note: the tail is the rear end

explanation.surface: Falling behind at the back of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail is to follow behind, lagging.

clue.text: One who lacks it has neither courage nor feeling

definitions.text: One who lacks it has neither courage nor feeling

parts.words: One who lacks it has neither courage nor feeling
parts.note: the missing quality supplies both boldness and physical sensation, so lacking it means lacking both

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a timid, numb person is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve means courage, and nerves carry sensation, so the word covers both.

clue.text: Remove minister with a position in governing class

indicators.note: position in says the minister and a are placed inside the governing class

parts.note: the elite is the ruling group

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a minister who holds a post in the ruling class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position in' signals the container; 'with' is a link joining the minister to 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to get rid of, a synonym.

clue.text: Hopeless pride-a sin needing correction

indicators.note: needing correction says the letters of pride-a sin must be put right in a new order

explanation.surface: Pride, a deadly sin, leaves someone without hope unless corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing correction' shuffles PRIDE A SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without hope is the state of despair, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Way to present Scripture, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for Scripture goes within the manner of speaking

parts.note: diction is one's style of enunciation
RE is religious education, the school subject once called Scripture

explanation.surface: A way to present Bible lessons, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to present' is a link. 'in a manner of speaking' looks like an idiom, but 'in' is the container signal and the rest is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A direction is a way one goes, a course.

clue.text: Paper-seller standing next to female East Ender

parts.note: one's station is one's social standing
a Cockney from London's East End drops the H, so her is 'er

explanation.surface: A newsagent stands beside a woman from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' is a link. A Cockney (an East Ender) drops the H, so 'her' becomes 'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer sells writing paper and office supplies.

clue.text: Quietens down frequently in Sunday School

indicators.note: in says the word for frequently sits inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: SS abbreviates Sunday School
frequently means often

explanation.surface: Things often calm down at Sunday school.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften is to become less harsh or loud, a synonym of calming.

clue.text: Unable to recall change of name as written

indicators.note: change of says the word name has its letters altered

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark something quoted as written

explanation.surface: Someone forgets a name change on a form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' signals the anagram, which gives the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesic describes memory loss, unable to remember.

clue.text: They are run by various ethnic groups

definitions.meaning: contests of speed, which athletes run

explanation.surface: Things organised by different communities.
explanation.definitionFit: Races are speed contests, and also groups of people of common descent.

clue.text: Valedictory toast

explanation.surface: A farewell toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is a British goodbye and also an old drinking salutation.

clue.text: Many writings establish belief in the saints

indicators.note: in says the belief is placed inside the saints' abbreviation

parts.note: SS abbreviates saints
a creed is a statement of belief

explanation.surface: Many texts set down faith in the saints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'establish' is a link; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Screeds are long pieces of writing.

clue.text: Mushrooms cause amusement to US soldier

parts.note: amusement is fun
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Mushrooms entertain an American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cause' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are examples of fungal growths.

clue.text: Disturbance always caused by a fraudster

parts.note: a racket is a loud disturbance
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A swindler always causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest business, a crook.

clue.text: Old magistrate gives note to a woman

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
Eve, the first woman, stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A former justice hands a message to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' and 'to a' are links. A reeve was a medieval English local official.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a chief officer of a town or district in medieval England, an old local magistrate.

clue.text: A piece of eel; very little eel

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tiny fragment of eel describes a very small eel.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel.

clue.text: Subjugate Eastern Slav in the North-East

indicators.note: in says the Slav goes within the North-East abbreviation

parts.note: NE abbreviates the North-East
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Eastern European is conquered in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern Slav' looks like one phrase but splits: the first word gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave is to bring under control, conquering.

clue.text: Not at all prosaic. Quite the opposite

definitions.meaning: written as poetry, in lines with metre

explanation.surface: Something is not prosaic at all; in fact, the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads as two words, in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is written in verse, and an inverse is the reverse of something.

clue.text: Hide away in south-eastern Mediterranean isle

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Hiding out on an island in the south-east Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete is to conceal, a synonym.

clue.text: The sound of new missiles

parts.note: arrows are missiles shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Describing the noise of fresh projectiles in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' is not noise but a strait of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow sea channel, and narrows are a strait.
